name: Thailand
tagline: Golden temples, longtail boats, and a 60-day visa-free welcome
hero_description: Thailand is the easiest big trip an Indian passport can take — visa-free for up to 60 days, a short flight away, and split neatly into two acts: Bangkok's gold-spired temples, mega-markets and street food, then the limestone-karst beaches of the Andaman coast at Phuket, Krabi and the Phi Phi islands.
best_time_to_visit: November to February for Bangkok and November to March for the Andaman beaches — dry, sunny and around 27°C; the islands' monsoon runs roughly May to October.

top_attractions.name: Grand Palace & Wat Phra Kaew, Bangkok
top_attractions.description: The royal complex founded in 1782, housing the Emerald Buddha — carved from a single block of green stone and re-robed seasonally by royal hands. Strict dress code applies.

top_attractions.name: Wat Arun
top_attractions.description: The 'Temple of Dawn' on the Chao Phraya river, its central spire studded with porcelain shards — best photographed at sunset from the opposite bank.

top_attractions.name: Wat Pho
top_attractions.description: Home to the 46-metre gold-plated Reclining Buddha and Thailand's traditional massage school — get an authentic Thai massage where it was codified.

top_attractions.name: Phi Phi Islands & Maya Bay
top_attractions.description: The Andaman's poster archipelago of sheer limestone karsts — Maya Bay reopened after a four-year reef-recovery closure and now runs on capped visitor numbers with no swimming in the bay itself.

top_attractions.name: Phang Nga Bay
top_attractions.description: Sea-canoe country: hidden lagoon caves and the needle rock of Khao Phing Kan, 'James Bond Island' since 1974's The Man with the Golden Gun.

top_attractions.name: Railay, Krabi
top_attractions.description: A beach peninsula sealed off by cliffs and reachable only by longtail boat — world-famous rock climbing above some of Thailand's finest sand.

activities: Chao Phraya temple day — Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun by river boat
Bangkok street-food night walk, from pad thai to mango sticky rice
Floating market and railway market day trip
Sea-canoeing the caves of Phang Nga Bay
Longtail ride to Railay's cliff-framed beaches
Thai cooking class or a traditional massage afternoon
Ethical elephant sanctuary visit (observation, no riding)
